subject: PrivInfra: least-privilege hardening for TF/Helm/Ansible modules
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Acme Energy - infra@acme.com, EdgeOps Consulting <eng@edgeops.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PrivInfra: least-privilege hardening for TF/Helm/Ansible modules

Hi team,

Following our kickoff call earlier this week, attaching the initial items we want to cover during the module hardening pass for Acme's private deployment (VPC + on-prem edge sites). Goal: get Terraform/Helm/Ansible modules to a baseline we can ship into Dedicated/Private without manual overrides.

TL;DR asks:
- Internal: please review the attached permissions spreadsheet and flag any provider/resource rows you think are under- or over-scoped.
- Acme/EdgeOps: confirm any constraints (existing on-prem KMS key ARNs, IP ranges) that would affect least-privilege bindings.
- All: agree on CI gating additions (terraform plan enforced, helm lint+policy, ansible dry-run checks) — see page 2 of the PDF.

High level priorities included in the attachments:
1) Enforcement of least-privilege IAM/service accounts per module (no broad roles at env-level).
2) Terraform state lock + fine-grained KMS CMK policy: ensure service accounts only decrypt for their envs.
3) Helm chart values defaults to disable elevated hostNetwork/podHostAccess and require networkPolicies by default for on-prem clusters.
4) Ansible roles -> run-as non-root, capability removal, and idempotent checks for network interface config.
5) CI: add an infra-scan job that fails PRs if policies regress (rego OPA + custom checks).

I've left inline comments on the spreadsheet for the modules we discussed: tf-modules/vpc, tf-modules/kms, helm/charts/edge-agent, ansible/roles/networking.

Next steps: can Karthik and Marcus pick the top three high-risk modules you want to gate first? I'd like to have a PR template for the hardening work by EOD Tuesday.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: priv-module-permissions.xlsx (spreadsheet), ci-gate-checklist.pdf (doc)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Energy - infra@acme.com, EdgeOps Consulting <eng@edgeops.io>
Date: Sat, 16 Aug 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivInfra: least-privilege hardening for TF/Helm/Ansible modules

Thanks Mina — good summary. Quick thoughts after skimming the sheet:

- Priority modules to gate first (my vote): tf-modules/k8s-cluster-auth, tf-modules/kms, tf-modules/networking (VPC peering & routing tables). These have the highest blast radius.
- For KMS: we should switch to per-environment aliases and update CMK policies so the TF service account has 'kms:Decrypt' only on the alias ARN. Avoid wildcard principals.
- Helm charts: add policy checks to prevent hostPath mounts in charts unless explicitly approved via an annotation. We should fail chart PRs by default in CI if hostPath or hostNetwork detected.
- Ansible: add a check that all roles set "become: false" unless an approved list is present; also require a verify-playbook step that runs --check against a staging VM.

PR pipeline change proposal (short):
1) terraform plan action must include workspace-aware state & show a 'permission delta' check (custom script compares current IAM bindings to the least-priv baseline).
2) helm lint + policy gate (chart-checker) with a documented opt-in process for exceptions.
3) ansible dry-run + static lint that fails on become/root commands in non-approved roles.

I'll draft the terraform and helm PR templates tonight and push to the privinfra repo. Marcus — can you validate the network modules for route table wide-open rules? I saw two places where 0.0.0.0/0 is still used for testing and needs a stronger guard.

-Karthik

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Acme Energy - infra@acme.com
Date: Sat, 16 Aug 2025 13:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivInfra: least-privilege hardening for TF/Helm/Ansible modules

On Sat, Aug 16, 2025 at 11:03 AM, Karthik Iyer wrote:
> - Priority modules to gate first (my vote): tf-modules/k8s-cluster-auth, tf-modules/kms, tf-modules/networking (VPC peering & routing tables). These have the highest blast radius.

Agreed. I ran a quick grep across the networking module and flagged two patterns:
- resource "aws_route" that still sets cidr_block = "0.0.0.0/0" in tf-modules/public-eip for 'testing' (file: tf-modules/public-eip/main.tf:78). We should change to a variable with no default and fail plan if left nil.
- Security groups: we have a convenience variable allow_from_any_ipv4 = true in some examples; remove or default to false and add a testing-only overlay.

EdgeOps: can you confirm the on-prem edge clusters' allowed CIDR ranges and the bastion host model? If we need to preserve NAT'ed ranges for certain sites we should document them and scope the TF inputs accordingly.

I pushed a small PR with a guard_that_fails.tf that aborts the plan when one of the unsafe patterns exists; it's a PoC (link: https://github.com/redwood/privinfra/pull/432). It needs review but can be used as a baseline for the CI gating job.

-Marcus

From: EdgeOps Consulting <eng@edgeops.io>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Energy - infra@acme.com
Date: Sat, 16 Aug 2025 17:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivInfra: least-privilege hardening for TF/Helm/Ansible modules

Hi Mina / team,

Thanks for the doc and the checklist. Quick answers from our side:
- On-prem KMS: Acme has two customer-managed keys we must support. We will provide full ARNs by Monday (they are not wildcards).
- Allowed CIDR ranges: Acme edge sites are using a mix of 10.40.0.0/16 and a NATed 172.20.x.x pool. We will list the exact /24s in a follow-up.
- Bastion model: current model uses per-site bastion (managed via Ansible), SSH jump user 'acme-admin', runs in a private subnet behind a NAT gateway. We agree to remove any plan that exposes RDP/SSH to 0.0.0.0/0.

We like Marcus's plan-guard idea; we can contribute a rego rule for the OPA policy that specifically rejects hostPath/hostNetwork and 0.0.0.0/0 in charts or TF route resources.

Action items from EdgeOps:
1) Provide KMS ARNs + exact CIDRs (by 2025-08-18).
2) Review PoC PR #432 and submit a rego rule.

- EdgeOps (Saira Bhatt)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Energy - infra@acme.com, EdgeOps Consulting <eng@edgeops.io>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 Aug 2025 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivInfra: least-privilege hardening for TF/Helm/Ansible modules

Thanks all — good progress. Quick status update and owners: 

- Karthik: draft terraform PR templates + kms policy snippet (due: 2025-08-19).
- Marcus: extend guard_that_fails.tf to cover aws_security_group ingress cidr checks + unit tests in terratest (due: 2025-08-20).
- Grace: helm chart policy integration with our chart-checker and add an exception workflow to the console docs (due: 2025-08-21).
- Olga (ops/security): can you schedule a threat review on 2025-08-22 10:00 AM PST and invite Acme and EdgeOps? We'll bring the attachments and PR links.
- EdgeOps/Acme: share KMS ARNs and exact CIDRs by 2025-08-18 so Marcus can finish the SG checks.

I've started a parent Jira (INFRA-1298) to track these workstreams and added the attachments to the ticket. Please use the PR template label 'priv-hardening' so we can easily find related PRs.

If anyone wants to propose a different staging model for the ansible verify-playbook (e.g., use ephemeral VMs or containerized VM emulation), add notes to the ticket — I'd prefer ephemeral VMs to reduce left-over state risk.

Mina
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
